Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

be quiet phrase

also hush, keep quiet, aw, keep quiet!, shut up, shut your mouth, keep your mouth shut, I’d better keep my mouth shut, why don’t you keep quiet?, why don’t you just shut up?, be silent, classroom commands, cut out the chatter, stop chattering, cut out the noise, stop that noise

classical

Traupman 33: be quiet, tacē (tacēte)

Tacē.

Other words

  • Quīn tacēs? — why don’t you keep quiet? (be quiet!)

    quīn with the indicative: an impatient “why not …?”, really a command · also used · classical · Plaut. Merc. 2.4.26: Quīn tacēs? — Mūtō imperās. (Lewis & Short s.v. mūtus); Traupman 106: why don’t you keep quiet?, quīn tū tacēs?

  • Obserā ōs tuum! — shut your mouth!

    also used · modern · Traupman 104: shut your mouth, obserā ōs tuum!; Traupman 107: shut up!, obserā ōs tuum!

    Traupman’s phrase, “bolt your mouth”. Lewis & Short has the figure with palātum, “to be silent” (Catull. 55.21), not with ōs; the everyday command is Tacē!.

  • silentium tenēre — keep silent

    silentium in the accusative; imperative silentium tenē (tenēte) · also used · classical · Liv. 5.9.4: tribūnī plēbis, cum invītī silentium tenuissent (Lewis & Short s.v. silentium); Traupman 33: be quiet, silentium tenē (tenēte)

Examples

  • Tacē, occultēmus lūmen et vōcem. — Licet.

    Hush, let’s hide the light and our voices. — All right; for a game in the dark.Plaut. Curc. 95

  • Au, tacē!

    Aw, keep quiet!Traupman 93

  • Taceam optimum est.

    I’d better keep my mouth shut.Traupman 104

  • Quīn tū tacē modo?

    Why don’t you just shut up?Traupman 107

  • Omitte (omittite) garrulitātem, quaesō.

    Cut out the chatter, please.Traupman 33

  • Omitte (omittite) strepitum, quaesō.

    Cut out the noise, please.Traupman 33

See also come here, shh!.
